key_insight: The paper extends deep energy methods to thermo-mechanical fracture by modeling a sharp crack directly in neural solvers, enabling coupled heat conduction, thermoelasticity, and crack growth without a phase-field length scale.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-efficient framework for predicting temperature-driven crack initiation and propagation in structures where thermal loading and mechanical stress interact.
method: Two neural networks learn temperature and displacement fields on a cracked domain.
A discontinuous scalar embedding lets fields jump across the sharp crack, while Williams-tip enrichment improves crack-tip accuracy.
Training minimizes incremental conduction and thermoelastic energy in a staggered scheme with Monte Carlo sampling refined near the crack tip.
evidence_signal: The method matches a published stress intensity factor for a stationary thermal edge crack to 0.11% and reproduces crack initiation and paths on graded and cruciform benchmark problems.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful crack-tip sampling, contour-radius checks for stress intensity factors, and accurate implementation of the sharp-crack embedding and tip enrichment.
paper_title: An extended deep energy method for thermo-mechanical crack propagation
